newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX range-trading after money supply data.
newsitem.headline: German DAX range-trading after money supply data.

text.p: Germany's DAX share index was seen trading in a range of between 3,000 and 3,030 after the latest German money supply data came out slightly higher than expected, scotching hopes of a quick interest rate cut.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares slipped 12.17 points to 3,016.50 in the first minutes of bourse trade.
December M3 money supply growth stood at an annual 7.9 percent compared to eight percent in November, but was nonetheless above market forecasts for a rate of 7.6 percent.
"The money supply figures were a shock," said one trader. March DAX futures slipped 13.5 points to 3,029.0.

Dealers also said there was some concern about details emerging on Germany's planned tax reform, with the Bonn government's tax working group saying earlier that it planned among other things to tighten rules on short-term gains from share sales.
"That acted as a dampener, largely because the market is in any case nervous," one trader.
The dollar's strength, trading at 1.6390 marks, was however seen exerting a positive effect on share values.
Among individual shares, engineering group Mannesmann was earlier riding high at 657.50 marks on speculation over its telecom business ahead of a news conference on the matter.
It later fell back to 647.50 marks, just 4.50 up on the day, as it emerged that its DBKom domestic communications joint venture, renamed as Arcor, would be investing some 800 million marks in 1997.
It also confirmed that U.S. telephone giant AT&T would be involved in the Arcor consortium.
